text:
Tampa Bay scored twice in the first period on shots worth 8 and 4 percent chances apiece, and that was enough to carry a game that Washington nearly played even from there. Charle-Edouard D'Astous opened the scoring 2:26 in, Conor Geekie made it 2-0 at 16:30, and both goals came off wrist shots set up by Brandon Hagel and Jake Guentzel. The Lightning also owned the opening 20 minutes by chance quality, 1.62 expected goals to 0.41.

After that, the game turned. Washington outchanced Tampa Bay 1.53 to 1.13 in the third and 2.13 to 1.97 over the final two periods, yet Justin Sourdif's tip-in in the second period, a 1 percent chance, was the only reward. Andrei Vasilevskiy faced 21 shots, stopped 20 and saved about 1.5 goals more than expected, and he was named first star. Guentzel sealed it at 17:55 of the third with a wrist shot, and the Lightning needed no power play to do it, going 0-for-3 with the man advantage and 0-for-2 for Washington.

The final read 3-1, but the underlying numbers were closer than that. Tampa Bay finished with 3.59 expected goals to Washington's 2.53, and in simulated replays of every shot the Lightning win 60 percent of the time. Hagel took six shots and had two assists, and Tampa Bay won 62 percent of faceoffs. Charlie Lindgren was good in defeat, saving roughly one goal more than expected on 29 shots.
